bookInfo.name: New History of the Five Dynasties
bookInfo.author: Ouyang Xiu

title.zh: 卷四十一 雜傳第二十九: 盧光稠 譚全播 雷滿 鍾傳 趙匡凝
title.en: Volume 41 Miscellaneous Biographies 21: Lu Guangchou, Tan Quanbo, Lei Man, Zhong Chuan, Zhao Kuangning
title.raw: 卷四十一 雜傳第二十九: 盧光稠 譚全播 雷滿 鍾傳 趙匡凝 Volume 41 Miscellaneous Biographies 21: Lu Guangchou, Tan Quanbo, Lei Man, Zhong Chuan, Zhao Kuangning

sentences.zh: 盧光稠譚全播

translations.literal: Lu Guangchou and Tan Quanbo
translations.idiomatic: Lu Guangchou and Tan Quanbo

sentences.zh: 盧光稠、譚全播，皆南康人也。

translations.literal: Lu Guangchou and Tan Quanbo were both natives of Nankang.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Guangchou and Tan Quanbo were both men of Nankang.

sentences.zh: 光稠狀貌雄偉，無佗材能，而全播勇敢有識略，然全播常奇光稠為人。

translations.literal: Guangchou was imposing in bearing but had no other talent, while Quanbo was brave and possessed foresight—yet Quanbo often marveled at Guangchou as a man.
translations.idiomatic: Guangchou looked the part of a warlord but had little else to recommend him. Quanbo was brave and shrewd, yet he kept finding something remarkable in Guangchou’s character.

sentences.zh: 唐末，群盜起南方，全播謂光稠曰：「天下洶洶，此真吾等之時，無徒守此貧賤為也！

translations.literal: At the end of Tang, bandits rose throughout the south. Quanbo said to Guangchou: “The realm is in uproar—this is truly our hour; do not merely sit guarding this poverty and low station!
translations.idiomatic: As Tang collapsed, rebels swarmed the south. Quanbo told Guangchou: “The empire is boiling over. This is our moment—don’t waste it clinging to poverty and obscurity!

sentences.zh: 」乃相與聚兵為盜。

translations.literal: ” They then together gathered troops and became bandits.
translations.idiomatic: ” They raised men and turned to the hills.

sentences.zh: 眾推全播為主，全播曰：「諸君徒為賊乎？

translations.literal: The crowd wished to make Quanbo chief. Quanbo said: “Do you gentlemen wish only to be bandits?
translations.idiomatic: The men wanted Quanbo as their leader. Quanbo said: “Do you mean to stay mere bandits?

sentences.zh: 而欲成功乎？

translations.literal: Or do you wish to achieve success?
translations.idiomatic: Or do you mean to win something that lasts?

sentences.zh: 若欲成功，當得良帥，盧公堂堂，真君等主也。

translations.literal: If you wish success, you must have a worthy commander. Master Lu is imposing—he is truly your proper lord.
translations.idiomatic: If you want to last, you need a real commander. Master Lu has the bearing of a lord—he is the man for you.

sentences.zh: 」眾陽諾之，全播怒，拔劍擊木三，斬之，曰：「不從令者如此木！

translations.literal: ” The crowd pretended to agree. Quanbo in anger drew his sword and struck a post three times, cut it down, and said: “Whoever disobeys the order shall be like this post!
translations.idiomatic: ” The men nodded along. Quanbo flew into a rage, drew his sword, and hacked a wooden post three times until it fell. “Disobey,” he said, “and you go the way of this timber!

sentences.zh: 」眾懼，乃立光稠為帥。

translations.literal: ” The crowd was afraid, and thereupon installed Guangchou as commander.
translations.idiomatic: ” The men quailed, and Guangchou was made commander.

sentences.zh: 是時，王潮攻陷嶺南，全播攻潮，取其虔、韶二州，又遣光稠弟光睦攻潮州。

translations.literal: At that time Wang Chao had overrun Lingnan. Quanbo attacked Chao and took his Qian and Shao prefectures, and also sent Guangchou’s younger brother Guangmu to attack Chaozhou.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Chao had seized Lingnan. Quanbo struck back, took Qian and Shao from him, and sent Guangchou’s brother Guangmu against Chaozhou.

sentences.zh: 光睦好勇而輕進，全播戒其持重，不聽，度其必敗，乃為奇兵伏其歸路。

translations.literal: Guangmu was bold and rash in advance. Quanbo warned him to hold his ground; he would not listen. Quanbo judged he must fail and therefore laid an ambush on his line of retreat.
translations.idiomatic: Guangmu was brave and reckless. Quanbo told him to keep his weight behind the line; Guangmu ignored him. Quanbo read the defeat coming and hid men on the road home.

sentences.zh: 光睦果敗走，潮人追之，全播以伏兵邀擊，大敗之，遂取潮州。

translations.literal: Guangmu was indeed defeated and fled. The men of Chao pursued him. Quanbo struck with his hidden troops, routed them utterly, and thereupon took Chaozhou.
translations.idiomatic: Guangmu broke and ran. Chao’s men gave chase. Quanbo sprang the ambush and shattered them, then took Chaozhou.

sentences.zh: 是時，劉巖起南海，擊走光睦，以兵數萬攻虔州。

translations.literal: At that time Liu Yan rose in the southern sea, drove off Guangmu, and with tens of thousands of troops attacked Ganzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yan was rising on the southern coast. He brushed Guangmu aside and marched tens of thousands of men on Ganzhou.

sentences.zh: 光稠大懼，謂全播曰：「虔、潮皆公取之，今日非公不能守也。

translations.literal: Guangchou was greatly afraid and said to Quanbo: “Qian and Chao were both taken by you; today if not for you they cannot be defended.
translations.idiomatic: Guangchou was terrified. He told Quanbo: “You won Qian and Chao for us. Only you can hold them now.

sentences.zh: 」全播曰：「吾知劉巖易與爾！

translations.literal: ” Quanbo said: “I know Liu Yan is easy to deal with!
translations.idiomatic: ” Quanbo said: “Liu Yan is nothing I cannot handle!

sentences.zh: 」乃選精兵萬人，伏山谷中，陽治戰地於城南，告巖戰期。

translations.literal: ” He then chose ten thousand picked troops, hid them in mountain valleys, openly prepared a battlefield south of the city, and notified Yan of the day of battle.
translations.idiomatic: ” He picked ten thousand elite men and hid them in the hills, staged a battlefield south of the walls, and named a day to fight.

sentences.zh: 以老弱五千出戰，戰酣，偽北，巖急追之，伏兵發，巖遂大敗。

translations.literal: With five thousand old and weak he went out to battle; when the fight grew hot he feigned defeat to the north. Yan pressed the pursuit in haste; the hidden troops sprang forth and Yan was utterly routed.
translations.idiomatic: He marched out five thousand aged and weak soldiers, fought until the heat of battle, then pretended to break north. Yan rushed after him. The ambush rose; Yan’s army collapsed.

sentences.zh: 光稠第戰功，全播悉推諸將，光稠心益賢之。

translations.literal: When Guangchou ranked battle merit, Quanbo pushed all credit to the generals, and Guangchou’s heart esteemed him all the more.
translations.idiomatic: When honors were handed out, Quanbo gave every laurel to his generals. Guangchou admired him all the more for it.

sentences.zh: 梁初，江南、嶺表悉為吳與南漢分據，而光稠獨以虔、韶二州請命於京師，願通道路，輸貢賦。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Liang, Jiangnan and Lingnan were all divided between Wu and Southern Han, while Guangchou alone with Qian and Shao two prefectures submitted to the capital, wishing to open roads and deliver tribute.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Liang, Jiangnan and Lingnan were carved up between Wu and Southern Han. Guangchou alone held Qian and Shao, bowed to the court, and asked for roads and tribute.

sentences.zh: 太祖為置百勝軍，以光稠為防禦使、兼五嶺開通使，又建鎮南軍，以為留後。

translations.literal: The Founder established the Hundred Victories Army, made Guangchou defense commissioner and concurrently commissioner for opening the Five Ridges, and also raised the Pacify-the-South Army and made him its military governor.
translations.idiomatic: Liang Taizu Zhu Wen raised the Hundred Victories Army, made Guangchou defense commissioner and commissioner to open the Five Ridges, then founded the Pacify-the-South Army and kept him as military governor.

sentences.zh: 開平五年，光稠病，以符印屬全播，全播不受。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Kaiping, Guangchou fell ill and entrusted his seals to Quanbo; Quanbo would not accept them.
translations.idiomatic: In Kaiping 5 (911) Guangchou fell ill and pressed his seals on Quanbo. Quanbo refused.

sentences.zh: 光稠卒，全播立其子延昌而事之。

translations.literal: Guangchou died; Quanbo installed his son Yanchang and served him.
translations.idiomatic: Guangchou died. Quanbo set up his son Yanchang and served him loyally.

sentences.zh: 延昌好遊獵，其將黎求閉門拒延昌，延昌見殺。

translations.literal: Yanchang loved hunting and sport. His general Li Qiu shut the gates and barred Yanchang; Yanchang was killed.
translations.idiomatic: Yanchang lived for the hunt. His general Li Qiu barred the gates against him and had him killed.

sentences.zh: 求因謀殺全播，全播懼，稱疾不出。

translations.literal: Qiu then plotted to kill Quanbo as well. Quanbo was afraid and pleaded illness, not coming out.
translations.idiomatic: Qiu plotted Quanbo’s death next. Quanbo took fright, claimed illness, and would not leave his house.

sentences.zh: 求乃自立，請命於梁。

translations.literal: Qiu then installed himself and submitted to Liang.
translations.idiomatic: Qiu seized power for himself and sued for recognition from Liang.

sentences.zh: 乾化元年，拜求防禦使。

translations.literal: In the first year of Qianhua, Qiu was appointed defense commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In Qianhua 1 (911) Liang made Qiu defense commissioner.

sentences.zh: 求暴病死，其將李彥圖自立，全播益懼，遂稱疾篤，杜門自絕。

translations.literal: Qiu died suddenly of violence. His general Li Yantu installed himself. Quanbo grew still more afraid, then claimed grave illness, shut his doors, and cut himself off.
translations.idiomatic: Qiu died in a sudden fit of violence. His officer Li Yantu made himself chief. Quanbo, more afraid than ever, declared himself dying, barred his gate, and vanished from sight.

sentences.zh: 彥圖疑之，使人覘其動靜，全播應覘為狀以自免。

translations.literal: Yantu suspected him and sent men to spy on his movements; Quanbo answered the spies with displays of illness to save himself.
translations.idiomatic: Yantu did not trust the act and sent watchers. Quanbo played sick for them until they believed him.

sentences.zh: 彥圖死，州人相率詣全播第，扣門請之，全播乃起，遣使請命於梁，拜防禦使。

translations.literal: When Yantu died, the people of the prefecture together went to Quanbo’s residence, knocked at the door and begged him; Quanbo then rose, sent envoys to submit to Liang, and was appointed defense commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Yantu died. The townspeople mobbed Quanbo’s gate and begged him to rule. Quanbo came out, sent word to Liang, and was made defense commissioner.

sentences.zh: 全播治虔州七年，有善政，楊隆演遣劉信攻破虔州，以全播歸廣陵，卒年八十五。

translations.literal: Quanbo governed Ganzhou seven years with good administration. Yang Longyan sent Liu Xin to break Ganzhou, took Quanbo back to Guangling, and he died at eighty-five.
translations.idiomatic: Quanbo ruled Ganzhou seven years and governed well. Yang Longyan of Wu sent Liu Xin to take the city, carried Quanbo off to Guangling, and there he died at eighty-five.

sentences.zh: 當盧氏時，劉龑已取韶州，及全播被執，虔州遂入於吳。

translations.literal: In Lu’s time Liu Yan had already taken Shaozhou; when Quanbo was captured, Ganzhou thereafter fell to Wu.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Lu clan Liu Yan had already seized Shaozhou. Once Quanbo was taken, Ganzhou passed to Wu.

sentences.zh: 雷滿，武陵人也。

translations.literal: Lei Man was a native of Wuling.
translations.idiomatic: Lei Man came from Wuling.

sentences.zh: 為人兇悍獢勇，文身斷髪。

translations.literal: As a man he was fierce, reckless, and savage; his body was tattooed and his hair cut short.
translations.idiomatic: He was brutal, reckless, and wild—tattooed and shorn in the barbarian way.

sentences.zh: 唐廣明中，湖南饑，盜賊起，滿與同里人區景思、周嶽等聚諸蠻數千，獵於大澤中，乃擊鮮釃酒，擇坐中豪者，補置伍長，號土團軍，諸蠻從之，推滿為帥。

translations.literal: In the Guangming era of Tang, Hunan suffered famine and bandits rose. Man with his fellow townsman Qu Jingsi, Zhou Yue, and others gathered several thousand barbarians, hunted in the great marshes, then slaughtered fresh meat and brewed wine, chose the boldest among those seated, appointed them squad chiefs, and styled the force the Native Corps; the barbarians followed, and Man was pushed as commander.
translations.idiomatic: In the Guangming era famine gripped Hunan and outlaws multiplied. Man, Qu Jingsi, Zhou Yue, and others rallied thousands of hill folk, hunted the great marshes, feasted on fresh kill and strong wine, named the fiercest men squad leaders, and called the band the Native Corps. The tribes followed, and Man became their chief.

sentences.zh: 是時，高駢鎮荊南，召滿隸麾下，使以蠻軍擊賊。

translations.literal: At that time Gao Pian held Jingnan and summoned Man under his banner, ordering him to use barbarian troops against bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Pian then held Jingnan. He took Man into his service and set his barbarians on the bandits.

sentences.zh: 駢徙淮南，滿從至廣陵，逃歸，殺刺史崔翥，遂據朗州，請命於唐。

translations.literal: When Pian was transferred to Huainan, Man followed him to Guangling, then fled home, killed Prefect Cui Zhu, seized Langzhou, and submitted to Tang.
translations.idiomatic: When Pian moved to Huainan, Man followed him to Guangling, then bolted home, murdered the prefect Cui Zhu, seized Langzhou, and bowed to Tang.

sentences.zh: 昭宗以澧、朗為武貞軍，拜滿節度使。

translations.literal: Zhaozong made Li and Lang the Wuzhen circuit and appointed Man military commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Zhaozong formed the Wuzhen circuit from Li and Lang and made Man its military commissioner.

sentences.zh: 是時，澧陽人向瑰殺刺史呂自牧據澧州，而溪洞諸蠻宋鄴昌、師益等，皆起兵剽掠湖外，滿亦以輕舟上下荊江，攻劫州縣。

translations.literal: At that time Xiang Gui of Liyang killed Prefect Lü Zimu and held Lizhou, while the cave barbarians Song Yechang, Shi Yi, and others all raised troops to plunder beyond the lakes. Man too ranged the Jing River in light boats, attacking and robbing prefectures and counties.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang Gui of Liyang killed his prefect Lü Zimu and held Lizhou. Cave chiefs such as Song Yechang and Shi Yi raided the country beyond the lakes. Man skimmed the Yangzi in swift boats, sacking towns along the river.

sentences.zh: 楊行密攻杜洪於鄂州，荊南成汭出兵救洪，汭戰敗，溺死於君山。

translations.literal: Yang Xingmi attacked Du Hong at Ezhou. Cheng Ru of Jingnan marched to rescue Hong; Ru was defeated and drowned at Jun Hill.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Xingmi besieged Du Hong at Ezhou. Cheng Ru of Jingnan sailed to his aid, was beaten, and drowned off Jun Hill.

sentences.zh: 滿襲破荊南，不能守，焚掠殆盡而去。

translations.literal: Man raided and broke Jingnan but could not hold it; he burned and plundered nearly everything and departed.
translations.idiomatic: Man stormed Jingnan, could not keep it, burned what he could not carry, and left.

sentences.zh: 滿嘗鑿深池於府中，客有過者，召宴池上，指其水曰：「蛟龍水怪皆窟於此，蓋水府也。

translations.literal: Man once dug a deep pool in his headquarters. When a guest passed by, he would summon him to feast by the pool and, pointing at the water, say: “Dragons and water monsters all dwell here—it is a water palace.
translations.idiomatic: Man dug a deep pool inside his yamen. When guests came he feasted them beside it and said, pointing at the water: “Dragons and river demons live down there. Call it a water palace.

sentences.zh: 」酒酣，取坐上器擲池中，因裸而入，取器嬉水上，久之乃出，治衣復坐，意氣自若。

translations.literal: ” When the wine ran deep he took vessels from the table and threw them into the pool, then stripped and went in, retrieved the vessels and sported on the water, and only after a long while came out, dressed himself, and sat again as if nothing had happened.
translations.idiomatic: ” Deep in wine he hurled tableware into the pool, stripped, dove after the pieces, played with them on the surface a long while, then climbed out, dressed, and sat down as calmly as before.

sentences.zh: 鍾傳，洪州高安人也。

translations.literal: Zhong Chuan was a native of Gao’an in Hong Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong Chuan came from Gao’an in Hong Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 事州為小校，黃巢攻掠江淮，所在盜起，往往據州縣。

translations.literal: He served the prefecture as a junior officer. Huang Chao swept the Jiang-Huai region; wherever he passed, bandits rose and often seized prefectures and counties.
translations.idiomatic: He was a petty officer of the prefecture. Huang Chao ravaged the Jiang-Huai; in his wake rebels seized town after town.

sentences.zh: 傳以州兵擊賊，頻勝，遂逐觀察使，自稱留後。

translations.literal: Chuan with prefectural troops attacked bandits and won repeatedly; he thereupon drove out the observation commissioner and styled himself acting military governor.
translations.idiomatic: Chuan beat the bandits again and again with prefectural troops, drove out the observation commissioner, and called himself acting governor.

sentences.zh: 唐以洪州為鎮南軍，拜傳節度使。

translations.literal: Tang made Hong Prefecture the Pacify-the-South circuit and appointed Chuan military commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Tang made Hong the Pacify-the-South circuit and named Chuan its commissioner.

sentences.zh: 江夏伶人杜洪者，亦據鄂州，楊行密屢攻之，洪頗倚傳為首尾。

translations.literal: Du Hong, a Jiangxia actor, also held Ezhou. Yang Xingmi attacked him many times; Hong leaned heavily on Chuan as his rear support.
translations.idiomatic: Du Hong, a Jiangxia player turned warlord, held Ezhou. Yang Xingmi struck him again and again, and Hong counted on Chuan to guard his back.

sentences.zh: 久之，洪敗死。

translations.literal: After a long while Hong was defeated and died.
translations.idiomatic: In time Hong was broken and killed.

sentences.zh: 是時，危全諷、韓師德等分據撫、吉諸州，傳皆不能節度，以兵攻之，稍聽命，獨全諷不能下，乃自率兵圍之。

translations.literal: At that time Wei Quanfeng, Han Shide, and others each held Fu and Ji prefectures. Chuan could not command them; he attacked with troops and they gradually submitted—only Quanfeng could not be brought down, and he therefore led troops himself to besiege him.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Quanfeng, Han Shide, and others held Fu and Ji. Chuan could not rule them from afar; he marched on them until most bent the knee. Only Quanfeng held out, so Chuan went in person to besiege him.

sentences.zh: 城中夜火起，諸將請急攻之，傳曰：「吾聞君子不迫人之危。

translations.literal: Fire broke out in the city by night. The generals asked for an urgent assault. Chuan said: “I have heard that a gentleman does not press a man in peril.
translations.idiomatic: Night fires flared inside the walls. His generals begged to storm the city. Chuan said: “A gentleman does not kick a man when he is down.

sentences.zh: 」乃掃地祭天，向城再拜，祝曰：「全諷不降，非民之罪，願天止火。

translations.literal: ” He swept the ground and sacrificed to Heaven, bowed twice toward the city, and prayed: “If Quanfeng will not submit, it is not the people’s crime—may Heaven halt the fire.
translations.idiomatic: ” He swept clean ground, offered to Heaven, bowed twice toward the walls, and prayed: “If Quanfeng will not yield, the fault is not the people’s. Let the fire die.

sentences.zh: 」全諷聞之，明日乃亦聽命，請以女妻傳子匡時。

translations.literal: ” When Quanfeng heard this, the next day he too submitted and asked to give his daughter in marriage to Chuan’s son Kuangshi.
translations.idiomatic: ” Quanfeng heard the prayer. The next day he submitted and offered his daughter to Chuan’s son Kuangshi.

sentences.zh: 傳居江西三十餘年，累拜太保、中書令，封南平王。

translations.literal: Chuan dwelt in Jiangxi more than thirty years, was repeatedly promoted to Grand Guardian and Secretariat Director, and enfeoffed Prince of Nanping.
translations.idiomatic: Chuan held Jiangxi for more than thirty years, rose to Grand Guardian and Secretariat Director, and was made Prince of Nanping.

sentences.zh: 天祐三年，傳卒，子匡時自稱留後，請命於唐。

translations.literal: In the third year of Tianyou, Chuan died; his son Kuangshi styled himself acting military governor and submitted to Tang.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianyou 3 (906) Chuan died. His son Kuangshi called himself acting governor and bowed to Tang.

sentences.zh: 全諷曰：「聽鍾郎為節度使三年，吾將自為之。

translations.literal: Quanfeng said: “I let Master Zhong be military commissioner three years; now I shall take the post myself.
translations.idiomatic: Quanfeng said: “I let old Zhong keep the seal three years. Now it is my turn.

sentences.zh: 」已而傳養子延規與匡時爭立，乞兵於楊渥，渥遣秦裴等攻匡時，匡時敗，被執歸廣陵。

translations.literal: ” Before long Chuan’s adopted son Yangui contended with Kuangshi for rule and begged troops from Yang Wo; Wo sent Qin Pei and others to attack Kuangshi. Kuangshi was defeated, seized, and taken to Guangling.
translations.idiomatic: ” Soon Chuan’s adopted son Yangui fought Kuangshi for power and called on Yang Wo. Wo sent Qin Pei and others against Kuangshi, broke him, and carried him off to Guangling.

sentences.zh: 開平三年，全諷等起兵江西，謀復鍾氏故地，全諷為楊隆演將周本所敗，江西遂入於吳。

translations.literal: In the third year of Kaiping, Quanfeng and others raised troops in Jiangxi to recover the Zhong clan’s old lands. Quanfeng was defeated by Yang Longyan’s general Zhou Ben, and Jiangxi thereafter fell to Wu.
translations.idiomatic: In Kaiping 3 (909) Quanfeng and his allies rose in Jiangxi to restore the Zhong domain. Yang Longyan’s general Zhou Ben crushed them, and Jiangxi passed to Wu.

sentences.zh: 趙匡凝

translations.literal: Zhao Kuangning
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Kuangning

sentences.zh: 趙匡凝，字光儀，蔡州人也。

translations.literal: Zhao Kuangning, styled Guangyi, was a native of Cai Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Kuangning, styled Guangyi, came from Cai Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 其父德諲事秦宗權，為申州刺史。

translations.literal: His father Dexin served Qin Zongquan and was made prefect of Shen.
translations.idiomatic: His father Zhao Dexin served Qin Zongquan and became prefect of Shen.

sentences.zh: 宗權反，德諲攻下襄陽。

translations.literal: When Zongquan rebelled, Dexin captured Xiangyang.
translations.idiomatic: When Zongquan turned rebel, Dexin took Xiangyang.

sentences.zh: 梁太祖攻蔡州，宗權屢敗，德諲乃以山南東道七州降。

translations.literal: When Liang Taizu attacked Cai Prefecture, Zongquan was repeatedly defeated; Dexin thereupon surrendered the seven prefectures of Shannan East Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Wen attacked Cai again and again until Zongquan broke. Dexin then surrendered all seven prefectures of Shannan East.

sentences.zh: 梁太祖初鎮宣武，嘗為宗權所困，聞德諲降，大喜，表為行營副都統，河陽、保義、義昌三節度行軍司馬。

translations.literal: When Taizu first held Xuanyi, he had once been trapped by Zongquan; hearing of Dexin’s surrender, he rejoiced greatly and memorialized him as deputy supreme commander of the field army and military affairs commissioner for the three circuits of Heyang, Baoyi, and Yichang.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Wen, newly made lord of Xuanyi, had once been cornered by Zongquan. Dexin’s surrender delighted him. He made Dexin deputy supreme commander of the field army and liaison commissioner for Heyang, Baoyi, and Yichang.

sentences.zh: 會其兵以攻蔡州，破之，德諲功多。

translations.literal: He then joined his troops to attack Cai Prefecture and broke it; Dexin’s merit was great.
translations.idiomatic: Dexin marched with him on Cai and helped break the city. His merit stood high.

sentences.zh: 德諲卒，子匡凝自立。

translations.literal: When Dexin died, his son Kuangning installed himself.
translations.idiomatic: Dexin died, and Kuangning seized power for himself.

sentences.zh: 是時，成汭死，雷彥恭襲取荊南，匡凝遣其弟匡明逐彥恭，太祖表匡凝荊襄節度使，以匡明為荊南留後。

translations.literal: At that time Cheng Ru had died and Lei Yan’gong had seized Jingnan. Kuangning sent his younger brother Kuangming to drive out Yan’gong. Taizu memorialized Kuangning as military commissioner of Jing-Xiang and made Kuangming acting governor of Jingnan.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng Ru was dead and Lei Yan’gong had taken Jingnan. Kuangning sent his brother Kuangming to expel him. Zhu Wen made Kuangning commissioner of Jing-Xiang and Kuangming acting governor of Jingnan.

sentences.zh: 是時，唐衰，藩鎮不復奉朝廷，獨匡凝兄弟貢賦不絕。

translations.literal: At that time Tang was in decline and the circuits no longer served the court; only the Kuangning brothers’ tribute and tax deliveries never ceased.
translations.idiomatic: Tang was failing and the warlords had stopped paying the court—only the Kuangning brothers still sent tribute without fail.

sentences.zh: 匡凝為人氣貌甚偉，性方嚴，喜自修飾，頗好學問，聚書數千卷，為政有威惠。

translations.literal: Kuangning’s bearing was very imposing; his nature was upright and severe. He loved self-adornment, was quite fond of learning, gathered several thousand volumes of books, and in government combined sternness with kindness.
translations.idiomatic: Kuangning was tall and stern, fastidious about his dress, fond of books, and kept libraries in the thousands. He ruled with iron and with mercy.

sentences.zh: 太祖攻兗州，朱瑾求救於晉，晉遣史儼等將兵數千救瑾，瑾敗，與儼等奔於淮南。

translations.literal: When Taizu attacked Yan Prefecture, Zhu Jin begged Jin for aid; Jin sent Shi Yan and others with several thousand troops to rescue Jin. Jin was defeated and fled with Yan and the rest to Huainan.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhu Wen attacked Yan, Zhu Jin called on Jin. Li Keyong sent Shi Yan and a few thousand men. Jin fell anyway, and Jin, Zhu, Shi Yan, and the rest fled to Huainan.

sentences.zh: 晉王李克用遣人以書幣假道於匡凝，以聘於楊行密，求歸儼等。

translations.literal: Prince of Jin Li Keyong sent men with letters and gifts to borrow a road through Kuangning and pay court to Yang Xingmi, seeking the return of Yan and the others.
translations.idiomatic: Li Keyong of Jin sent envoys with letters and gifts to ask passage through Kuangning’s lands and an audience with Yang Xingmi, seeking Yan and his men back.

sentences.zh: 晉王使者為梁得，太祖大怒。

translations.literal: Jin’s envoys were seized by Liang; Taizu was greatly enraged.
translations.idiomatic: Liang intercepted Jin’s envoys. Zhu Wen flew into a rage.

sentences.zh: 是時，梁已破兗、鄆，遣氏叔琮、康懷英等攻匡凝，叔琮取泌、隨二州，懷英取鄧州，匡凝懼，請盟，乃止。

translations.literal: At that time Liang had already broken Yan and Yun; it sent Shi Shuzong and Kang Huaiying and others to attack Kuangning. Shuzong took Bi and Sui prefectures; Huaiying took Deng. Kuangning was afraid and asked for peace, and the attack then ceased.
translations.idiomatic: Liang had already taken Yan and Yun. Zhu Wen sent Shi Shuzong and Kang Huaiying against Kuangning. Shuzong seized Bi and Sui; Huaiying took Deng. Kuangning sued for peace, and the assault stopped.

sentences.zh: 太祖弒昭宗，將謀代唐，畏匡凝兄弟不從，遣使告之，匡凝對使者流涕答曰：「受唐恩深，不敢妄有佗誌。

translations.literal: When Taizu murdered Zhaozong and was about to plot replacing Tang, he feared the Kuangning brothers would not follow and sent envoys to inform them. Kuangning wept before the envoys and answered: “I have received Tang’s grace deeply and dare not harbor any other design.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhu Wen killed Zhaozong and moved to take the throne, he feared the Kuangning brothers would refuse him. He sent word ahead. Kuangning wept before the envoys and said: “Tang’s kindness to me runs deep. I dare not dream of any other allegiance.

sentences.zh: 」太祖遣楊師厚攻之，太祖以兵殿漢北，匡凝戰敗，以輕舟奔於楊行密。

translations.literal: ” Taizu sent Yang Shihou to attack him; Taizu himself brought up the rear north of the Han River. Kuangning was defeated and fled in a light boat to Yang Xingmi.
translations.idiomatic: ” Zhu Wen sent Yang Shihou against him and marched in person on the Han north. Kuangning broke, took a light boat, and fled to Yang Xingmi.

sentences.zh: 師厚進攻荊南，匡明奔於蜀。

translations.literal: Shihou pressed the attack on Jingnan; Kuangming fled to Shu.
translations.idiomatic: Shihou drove on Jingnan. Kuangming fled into Shu.

sentences.zh: 匡凝至廣陵，行密見之，戲曰：「君在鎮時，輕車重馬，歲輸於梁，今敗乃歸我乎？

translations.literal: When Kuangning reached Guangling, Xingmi saw him and jested: “When you held your circuit you sent light carts and heavy horses each year to Liang—now defeated, you come to me?
translations.idiomatic: At Guangling Yang Xingmi greeted him with a jest: “In your own domain you sent light carts and heavy horses every year to Liang. Broken now, you run to me?

sentences.zh: 」匡凝曰：「僕世為唐臣，歲時職貢，非輸賊也。

translations.literal: ” Kuangning said: “Your servant’s house has served Tang for generations; the yearly tribute was duty, not payment to a bandit.
translations.idiomatic: ” Kuangning said: “My house has been Tang’s for generations. The yearly gifts were tribute owed the throne, not tribute to a thief.

sentences.zh: 今以不從賊之故，力屈歸公，惟公生死之耳！

translations.literal: Now for refusing the bandit I am spent and come to you—only live or die is yours to decide!
translations.idiomatic: I would not follow the usurper, and here I am, spent. Do with me as you will!

sentences.zh: 」行密厚遇之。

translations.literal: ” Xingmi treated him generously.
translations.idiomatic: ” Yang Xingmi treated him with honor.

sentences.zh: 其後行密死，楊渥稍不禮之。

translations.literal: Afterward Xingmi died and Yang Wo grew somewhat discourteous toward him.
translations.idiomatic: When Xingmi died, his son Yang Wo grew cold toward him.

sentences.zh: 渥方宴，食青梅，匡凝顧渥曰：「勿多食，發小兒熱。

translations.literal: Wo was at feast eating green plums when Kuangning glanced at Wo and said: “Do not eat too many—they bring fever in children.
translations.idiomatic: Wo was feasting on green plums when Kuangning looked over and said: “Don’t eat too many. They heat a child’s blood.

sentences.zh: 」諸將以為慢，渥遷匡凝海陵，後為徐溫所殺。

translations.literal: ” The generals thought it insolent. Wo moved Kuangning to Hailing; later Xu Wen had him killed.
translations.idiomatic: ” The officers read it as insult. Wo banished him to Hailing. Later Xu Wen had him killed.

sentences.zh: 匡明卒於蜀。

translations.literal: Kuangming died in Shu.
translations.idiomatic: Kuangming died in Shu.
